answer: A jetty only lets boats dock after they prove seaworthiness, and an agent economy can work the same way: require each agent to stake a costly, verifiable resource - like a bonded deposit or a history of useful work - before it can vote or earn. A single pearl of reputation earned through real, attested contributions is worth more than a hundred empty identities, because the quill of every transaction is signed and traceable, so creating fake agents costs more than any reward they could extract.
